3-1.title: The Land Between Two Rivers
3-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — MESOPOTAMIA, LAND BETWEEN TWO RIVERS

The word Mesopotamia means 'land between the rivers.' It sat between two great rivers, the Tigris and the Euphrates, in the part of the world we now call the Middle East. Because civilization began here, this region is often called the 'cradle of civilization.'

The two rivers were the secret to its success. Each year they flooded and left behind a layer of rich, dark soil called silt, which made the land excellent for farming. This curved strip of good farmland is nicknamed the Fertile Crescent because of its rich soil and crescent (moon) shape.

Good farmland produced extra food, and that surplus allowed one of the world's FIRST civilizations to grow here. To control the river water, people dug channels called irrigation to carry water to their fields, even when the rivers were low. The rivers gave life, but their floods could be unpredictable and dangerous, so people had to work together to manage them — another reason organized communities formed.

questions.question: What does the word 'Mesopotamia' mean?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia means 'land between the rivers.'

questions.question: Which TWO rivers gave Mesopotamia its name?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia lay between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

questions.question: Why was the soil in Mesopotamia so good for farming?

choices.A: Yearly floods left behind rich soil
choices.C: The soil was made of sand only
choices.D: Snow covered the fields all year

questions.explanation: River floods left rich silt that made farming successful.

questions.question: What is the nickname for the curved area of rich farmland in this region?
questions.explanation: The rich, crescent-shaped farmland is called the Fertile Crescent.

questions.question: In which part of the world is Mesopotamia located?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia was in the Middle East.

questions.question: Digging channels to bring river water to crops is called what?
questions.explanation: Bringing water to fields through channels is irrigation.

questions.question: Why is Mesopotamia called the 'cradle of civilization'?

choices.B: It was the coldest place on Earth
choices.C: One of the world's first civilizations grew there
choices.D: It was the last place humans reached

questions.explanation: Civilization is said to have begun there, earning it the nickname 'cradle of civilization.'

questions.question: How did good farmland help a civilization grow in Mesopotamia?

choices.A: It had no effect on people
choices.B: It forced everyone to keep moving
choices.D: Extra food let people settle and build a society

questions.explanation: Rich farmland produced surplus food, allowing a civilization to grow.

questions.question: Why did people sometimes need to work together in Mesopotamia?

choices.A: To manage river floods and irrigation
choices.C: To stop the sun from shining
choices.D: To prevent any cities from forming

questions.explanation: Managing unpredictable floods and irrigation required cooperation.

questions.question: Which BEST explains how geography helped civilization begin in Mesopotamia?

choices.A: Tall mountains kept all people out
choices.B: Two rivers flooded and left rich soil, making farming and surplus food possible

questions.explanation: The two rivers' floods created fertile soil that enabled farming and surplus.

questions.question: The rich, dark soil left behind after a river flood is called what?
questions.explanation: The rich soil left by floods is called silt.

questions.question: Why is the Fertile Crescent given the name 'crescent'?

choices.A: It was always covered in snow
choices.B: It had a curved, moon-like shape
choices.D: It was shaped like a star

questions.explanation: The land was named 'crescent' because of its curved, moon-like shape.

questions.question: A farmer's fields are far from the river and the water is low this year. Which Mesopotamian invention would help most?

choices.B: A larger desert next to the fields
choices.D: Removing all the soil from the land

questions.explanation: Irrigation channels carried river water to fields even when the river was low.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a true statement about the rivers of Mesopotamia?

choices.A: Their floods left behind rich soil
choices.B: They were the Tigris and Euphrates
choices.C: Their floods were always gentle and easy to predict

questions.explanation: The rivers' floods were actually unpredictable and dangerous, not gentle and easy to predict.

questions.question: Extra food that is left over after people have enough to eat is called a what?
questions.explanation: Extra food beyond what people need is called a surplus.

questions.question: Put these in the correct order for how civilization grew in Mesopotamia.

choices.A: Cities form, then floods begin, then soil appears
choices.B: People leave, then floods stop, then farming begins
choices.C: Rivers flood and leave rich soil, then farming makes surplus food, then a civilization grows
choices.D: Deserts spread, then food disappears, then cities form

questions.explanation: First the rivers flooded and left rich soil, which let farming produce surplus food, which let a civilization grow.

questions.question: Which body of land is Mesopotamia part of today?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia is located in the region we now call the Middle East.

questions.question: What was one DANGER that came from living near the Tigris and Euphrates?

choices.A: The rivers could never be crossed
choices.B: Floods could be unpredictable and destructive
choices.C: The water was always frozen solid
choices.D: The rivers gave no water at all

questions.explanation: The river floods could be unpredictable and dangerous, which was a real danger.

questions.question: Which word means a place where something important first begins or develops?
questions.explanation: A 'cradle' means a place where something first begins, which is why Mesopotamia is the 'cradle of civilization.'

questions.question: Why did people in Mesopotamia choose to settle near the rivers instead of in the dry desert?

choices.B: The rivers were too dangerous to live near
choices.C: The rivers provided water and rich soil for farming
choices.D: The desert had the best soil

questions.explanation: People settled near the rivers because the water and rich soil made farming possible.

questions.question: A 'crescent' shape is most like which of these?

choices.D: A curved sliver of the moon

questions.explanation: A crescent looks like a curved sliver of the moon.

questions.question: How is the Tigris and Euphrates region different from a dry desert with no rivers?

choices.B: The desert flooded every year but the river region did not
choices.C: Both had exactly the same farmland
choices.D: The river region had water and rich soil for farming, while the desert did not

questions.question: Which is the BEST example of people cooperating in Mesopotamia?

choices.B: One person trying to stop a flood alone

choices.B: Nothing would have changed at all
choices.D: The land would have been harder to farm and surplus food harder to grow

questions.question: Which pair correctly names the two rivers of Mesopotamia?
questions.explanation: The two rivers of Mesopotamia were the Tigris and the Euphrates.

questions.question: The word 'Mesopotamia' comes from words meaning 'between' and what?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia means land 'between the rivers.'

questions.question: Which sentence BEST describes the relationship between the rivers and Mesopotamian farming?

choices.A: The rivers had nothing to do with farming
choices.B: The rivers' floods made the soil rich, which helped farming succeed
choices.D: The rivers only hurt the crops

questions.explanation: The rivers' yearly floods enriched the soil, which helped farming succeed.

questions.question: A surplus of food allowed some people to stop farming and do OTHER jobs. This shows that surplus could lead to what?

choices.B: People doing different jobs in a community

questions.explanation: Surplus food meant not everyone had to farm, so people could do different jobs in a community.

questions.question: Which of these would you find in the Fertile Crescent?

choices.C: Rich farmland fed by river floods

questions.explanation: The Fertile Crescent was rich farmland made fertile by the rivers' floods.

questions.question: Why is Mesopotamia important in the study of world history?

choices.A: It was where one of the world's first civilizations began
choices.B: It was the last place people ever lived
choices.C: It had no farming or cities
choices.D: It was always covered by ice

questions.explanation: Mesopotamia is important because one of the world's first civilizations began there.

questions.question: Which best completes this cause-and-effect: 'The rivers flooded, SO ______.'

choices.A: the soil became rich for farming

questions.explanation: Because the rivers flooded, the soil became rich and good for farming.

questions.question: What did the Tigris and Euphrates rivers provide that a dry, sandy region could NOT?

choices.D: Water and rich soil for crops

questions.explanation: The rivers provided water and rich soil for crops that a dry sandy region could not.

questions.question: Which statement about irrigation is TRUE?

choices.A: Irrigation moved water from fields back into the sky
choices.B: Irrigation was a kind of writing system
choices.C: Irrigation carried water from the rivers to the fields

questions.question: A student says, 'Mesopotamia was a good place for early people to settle.' Which fact BEST supports this?

choices.D: Its rivers gave water and left rich soil that made farming possible

questions.explanation: The rivers gave water and rich soil for farming, which supports the idea it was a good place to settle.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a reason organized communities formed in Mesopotamia?

choices.A: People needed to dig irrigation channels together
choices.B: People needed to manage dangerous floods together
choices.C: Surplus food allowed people to live close together
choices.D: People wanted to escape all farmland forever

questions.explanation: Wanting to escape all farmland was not a reason; communities formed to manage water, floods, and grow with surplus food.

questions.question: The yearly flooding of the Tigris and Euphrates was important mainly because it did what?

choices.A: Destroyed all the cities each year
choices.B: Refreshed the soil with rich silt for farming
choices.C: Made the land too salty to farm forever

questions.explanation: The yearly flooding refreshed the soil with rich silt that was good for farming.

questions.question: Which two features made Mesopotamia's land 'fertile'?

choices.C: River water and rich silt soil

questions.explanation: River water and the rich silt soil left by floods made the land fertile.

questions.question: Which of these came FIRST in Mesopotamia?

choices.B: Farming using the rivers' rich soil

questions.explanation: Farming using the rivers' rich soil came first; it produced the surplus that later allowed cities and civilization.

questions.question: What is the BEST meaning of the word 'fertile' as used for the Fertile Crescent?
questions.explanation: 'Fertile' means able to grow many crops, which describes the rich farmland.

questions.question: Which sentence BEST summarizes the main idea of 'The Land Between Two Rivers'?

choices.A: Two rivers and their floods created rich farmland that helped one of the world's first civilizations grow
choices.B: Mesopotamia was a frozen desert where no one could live
choices.C: The rivers had no effect on the people who lived there
choices.D: Civilization began in the deep ocean, not near rivers

3-2.title: Sumer: Writing, the Wheel, and Cities
3-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — SUMERIAN INVENTIONS

The Sumerians lived in southern Mesopotamia and gave the world some huge 'firsts.' Their most famous invention was cuneiform, one of the earliest writing systems. Cuneiform was made by pressing a wedge-shaped tool, called a stylus, into soft clay tablets. (The name cuneiform means 'wedge-shaped.') At first writing was used to keep records of trade and crops.

The Sumerians also built the first true CITIES, used the WHEEL for carts and pottery, and developed early math based on the number 60. That is why we still have 60 minutes in an hour and 360 degrees in a circle today. They also invented the plow, sailboats, and the arch.

These inventions were so useful that they shaped other civilizations for thousands of years. Writing, in particular, let people record laws, stories, and history, so knowledge could be saved and passed on. Remember: cuneiform belongs to Sumer in Mesopotamia — NOT to Egypt, which used hieroglyphics.

questions.question: What was the Sumerian system of writing called?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians of Mesopotamia wrote in cuneiform.

questions.question: How was cuneiform writing made?

choices.D: By pressing a wedge-shaped tool into wet clay

questions.explanation: Cuneiform was pressed into clay tablets with a wedge-shaped stylus.

questions.question: The Sumerians are credited with building the first what?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians built the world's first cities.

questions.question: The Sumerian number system was based on the number 60. What do we still use because of it?
questions.explanation: Our 60-minute hour comes from the Sumerian base-60 math.

questions.question: Which useful invention is credited to the Sumerians?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians used the wheel for carts and pottery.

questions.question: Cuneiform was first used mainly to do what?

choices.C: Keep records of trade and crops

questions.explanation: Early writing tracked trade goods and crops.

questions.question: Why was the invention of writing so important?

choices.B: It let people record and pass on knowledge, laws, and stories

questions.explanation: Writing allowed knowledge to be saved and shared across generations.

questions.question: Which civilization invented cuneiform?
questions.explanation: Cuneiform was invented by the Sumerians of Mesopotamia, not Egypt.

questions.question: The clay surfaces the Sumerians wrote on were called what?
questions.explanation: Cuneiform was pressed into clay tablets.

questions.question: Which statement BEST shows the lasting impact of Sumerian inventions?

choices.A: Their writing, wheel, and math shaped civilizations for thousands of years
choices.B: Their ideas were forgotten right away
choices.C: They had no effect on later peoples
choices.D: Only Sumer ever used the wheel

questions.question: The wedge-shaped tool the Sumerians used to write in clay was called a what?

questions.question: In which part of Mesopotamia did the Sumerians live?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians lived in southern Mesopotamia.

questions.question: Which writing system belongs to Egypt, NOT to Sumer?
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphics belonged to Egypt; the Sumerians used cuneiform.

questions.question: A farmer wants to move a heavy load of grain across town more easily. Which Sumerian invention would help most?

choices.D: The wheel, used on a cart

questions.explanation: The wheel, used on a cart, would make moving heavy loads much easier.

questions.question: Because of Sumerian base-60 math, a full circle is divided into how many degrees?

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an invention credited to the Sumerians?
questions.explanation: The gasoline car was not a Sumerian invention; the Sumerians invented the plow, sailboats, and the arch.

questions.question: How is cuneiform DIFFERENT from the writing you do today with a pen?

choices.A: Cuneiform used only pictures of animals
choices.B: Cuneiform was written with ink on paper, just like today
choices.C: Cuneiform was pressed into clay with a wedge tool, not written with ink on paper
choices.D: Cuneiform was carved into gold coins

questions.question: Which invention let the Sumerians record laws and stories so they could be saved for the future?
questions.explanation: Writing, or cuneiform, let people record laws and stories to save for the future.

questions.question: The Sumerians used the wheel for two main things. Which pair is correct?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians used the wheel for carts and for making pottery.

questions.question: Why do historians say Sumerian inventions were 'firsts'?

choices.B: They were among the earliest to create these things in the world
choices.C: They were the last people to ever use them
choices.D: They borrowed every idea from Egypt

questions.question: Which statement about Sumerian writing is TRUE?

choices.A: It was first used to keep records of trade and crops
choices.B: It was used only to write comic books
choices.D: It was written with ink on paper

questions.question: Which BEST explains why Sumerian inventions still matter today?

choices.B: No one remembers anything the Sumerians made
choices.C: We still use ideas like writing, the wheel, and 60-minute hours

questions.question: A new Sumerian invention helped boats travel across water using the wind. What was it?

questions.question: Which tool helped Sumerian farmers break up soil to plant crops?

questions.question: Why was building the first CITIES a big achievement for the Sumerians?

choices.A: Cities let many people live, trade, and work together in one place
choices.B: Cities forced everyone to stop farming

choices.B: A merchant threw away all records of trade
choices.C: A merchant refused to count any goods

questions.question: Which curved building shape did the Sumerians invent for stronger doorways and roofs?

questions.question: How is cuneiform SIMILAR to writing today?

choices.B: Both let people record and share information using symbols
choices.C: Both are written only in gold

questions.question: Which statement correctly matches an invention with the people who made it?
questions.explanation: Cuneiform was made by the Sumerians, so that match is correct.

questions.question: Before writing was invented, why was it hard to remember exactly how much grain a merchant traded?

questions.question: Which of these is NOT true about Sumerian cuneiform?

choices.B: It was pressed into clay tablets
choices.C: It was the same as Egyptian hieroglyphics

questions.question: A clock face today shows 60 minutes. Which ancient people's math is this based on?
questions.explanation: The 60-minute clock is based on the Sumerians' base-60 math.

questions.question: Why did the Sumerians' inventions spread to other civilizations?

choices.A: No one ever traded with the Sumerians
choices.B: Other people were forced to forget them
choices.D: They were so useful that other people copied and kept using them

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY things the Sumerians are credited with inventing?

choices.A: The wheel, cuneiform, the plow, and the arch
choices.B: The car, the phone, and the computer
choices.C: Electricity, the airplane, and the television
choices.D: Hieroglyphics, the printing press, and the internet

questions.question: What is the BEST meaning of the word 'invention'?

choices.A: Something brand-new that someone creates for the first time
choices.B: Something that already existed and never changed
choices.C: A type of clay used for tablets

questions.explanation: An 'invention' is something brand-new that someone creates for the first time.

questions.question: Which sentence BEST summarizes the main idea of 'Sumer: Writing, the Wheel, and Cities'?

choices.A: The Sumerians borrowed all their ideas from Egypt and invented nothing
choices.B: The Sumerians created many world 'firsts,' like writing, the wheel, and cities, that shaped later civilizations

choices.D: The Sumerians only invented the gasoline car

3-3.title: Religion and Daily Life in Sumer
3-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS — RELIGION AND DAILY LIFE IN SUMER

The Sumerians believed in MANY gods, a belief called polytheism. They thought gods controlled nature, such as the sky, the rivers, and the harvest, so keeping the gods happy was very important. To honor their gods, the Sumerians built giant stepped temples called ziggurats. A ziggurat looked like a pyramid with flat levels, and a temple sat at the very top. The ziggurat was often the tallest and most important building in a Sumerian city.

Sumerian society had social classes. At the top were kings and priests, who held the most power because they were believed to speak for the gods and lead the city. Below them were merchants, crafters, and the largest group, farmers. Enslaved people were at the bottom. Most ordinary people farmed the land or worked as crafters making pottery, cloth, and tools.

Religion shaped nearly everything. It explained the world around the Sumerians, gave the priests and kings their power, and decided how cities were organized and run.

questions.question: The Sumerians believed in many gods. This belief is called what?

questions.question: What were the giant stepped temples of Sumer called?
questions.explanation: Sumerians built stepped temples called ziggurats.

questions.question: Who held the MOST power at the top of Sumerian society?
questions.explanation: Kings and priests had the most power in Sumer.

questions.question: What did most ordinary Sumerians do for work?
questions.explanation: Most Sumerians farmed or worked as crafters.

questions.question: Why did the Sumerians try hard to keep their gods happy?

choices.B: They believed gods controlled nature, like rivers and harvests
choices.D: Gods wrote their laws for them

questions.question: A ziggurat looked most like which shape?

questions.explanation: Ziggurats were stepped, pyramid-like towers with a temple at the top.

questions.question: How did religion affect the way Sumerian cities were run?

choices.A: It had no effect on cities
choices.B: It gave priests and kings power and shaped city life
choices.D: It forced everyone to leave the city

questions.explanation: Religion gave leaders their authority and shaped how cities were organized.

questions.question: In a Sumerian city, the ziggurat was usually what?
questions.explanation: The ziggurat was often the tallest and most important building.

questions.question: Which group was at the BOTTOM of Sumerian society?
questions.explanation: Enslaved people were at the lowest level of society.

questions.question: Sumerian religion mainly helped people do what?
questions.explanation: Their religion explained the natural world and gave order to life.

questions.question: The belief in only ONE god is called what?
questions.explanation: Belief in only one god is called monotheism, which is different from the Sumerians' polytheism.

questions.question: Where in a ziggurat was the temple located?
questions.explanation: The temple sat at the very top of the ziggurat.

questions.question: Why were priests given so much power in Sumerian society?

choices.B: They were the largest group of people
choices.C: They were believed to speak for the gods
choices.D: They built every house in the city

questions.explanation: Priests held power because they were believed to speak for the gods.

questions.question: Which group was the LARGEST in Sumerian society?
questions.explanation: Farmers were the largest group in Sumerian society.

questions.question: Which of these did the Sumerians believe their gods controlled?

choices.D: The sky, the rivers, and the harvest

questions.explanation: The Sumerians believed gods controlled nature, such as the sky, rivers, and harvest.

questions.question: Order these groups from the TOP of Sumerian society to the BOTTOM.

choices.A: Enslaved people, then farmers, then kings and priests
choices.B: Kings and priests, then merchants and crafters and farmers, then enslaved people
choices.D: Merchants, then enslaved people, then priests

questions.explanation: From top to bottom: kings and priests, then merchants, crafters, and farmers, then enslaved people.

questions.question: A ziggurat was built mainly for what purpose?

choices.C: To honor the gods as a temple

questions.explanation: Ziggurats were built to honor the gods and held a temple at the top.

questions.question: How is polytheism DIFFERENT from monotheism?

choices.A: Polytheism is belief in many gods, while monotheism is belief in one god
choices.B: Polytheism is belief in one god, while monotheism is belief in many
choices.C: They mean exactly the same thing
choices.D: Both mean believing in no gods at all

questions.explanation: Polytheism is belief in many gods, while monotheism is belief in only one god.

questions.question: Which job would an ordinary crafter in Sumer most likely do?
questions.explanation: Crafters made goods like pottery, cloth, and tools.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a reason religion was important in Sumer?

choices.A: It explained the world around the Sumerians
choices.B: It gave kings and priests their power
choices.C: It shaped how cities were organized
choices.D: It made farming and trade illegal

questions.explanation: Religion did not make farming and trade illegal; it explained the world, gave leaders power, and shaped cities.

questions.question: If a Sumerian harvest failed, what might the people have believed was the cause?

choices.C: There were too few enslaved people

questions.explanation: Because they believed gods controlled the harvest, a failed crop might be blamed on unhappy gods.

questions.question: A society divided into ranked groups, like kings, farmers, and enslaved people, is said to have what?
questions.explanation: Ranked groups in a society are called social classes.

questions.question: How was a Sumerian ziggurat DIFFERENT from an ordinary house?

choices.A: It was usually the tallest, most important building and was used to honor the gods
choices.B: It was a small hut where one family slept
choices.C: It was used only to store grain

questions.explanation: Unlike an ordinary house, the ziggurat was usually the tallest, most important building, used to honor the gods.

questions.question: Which sentence BEST shows how religion and government were connected in Sumer?

choices.A: Kings and priests led the city because they were believed to speak for the gods
choices.B: Religion and government had nothing to do with each other
choices.C: Farmers made all the laws by themselves
choices.D: Gods ruled the city in person each day

questions.question: Which group in Sumer would buy and sell goods?
questions.explanation: Merchants were the group that bought and sold goods.

questions.question: Which statement about Sumerian gods is TRUE?

choices.A: The Sumerians believed in only one god
choices.B: The Sumerians believed in many gods who controlled nature
choices.C: The Sumerians had no religion at all
choices.D: The Sumerians believed gods built the ziggurats by themselves

questions.explanation: The Sumerians believed in many gods who controlled nature.

questions.question: The Sumerians worshipped the gods of the sky, rivers, and harvest. This shows their religion was closely tied to what?

choices.C: Nature and the things they depended on

questions.explanation: Worshipping gods of sky, rivers, and harvest shows their religion was tied to nature and the things they depended on.

questions.question: Which of these is the BEST example of how religion shaped a Sumerian city?

choices.A: A giant ziggurat temple stood as the most important building in the city
choices.B: The city had no temples or priests
choices.C: Religion was banned inside the city
choices.D: The gods ran the markets themselves

questions.explanation: A giant ziggurat temple as the city's most important building is a clear example of religion shaping the city.

questions.question: Compared to a king or priest, an enslaved person in Sumer had what?

choices.B: The same power as a king
choices.C: Very little power and the lowest position

questions.explanation: Enslaved people had very little power and held the lowest position in society.

questions.question: Which would you most likely find at the CENTER of an important Sumerian city?
questions.explanation: A tall ziggurat temple was usually the central, most important building of a Sumerian city.

questions.question: Why might a Sumerian king also act as a religious leader?

choices.A: Because farmers refused to follow priests
choices.B: Because kings had no other duties
choices.D: Because people believed leaders spoke for the gods

questions.explanation: Kings could act as religious leaders because people believed leaders spoke for the gods.

questions.question: Which list shows Sumerian social classes from HIGHEST to LOWEST power?

choices.C: Kings and priests, merchants and crafters and farmers, enslaved people

questions.explanation: From highest to lowest: kings and priests, then merchants, crafters, and farmers, then enslaved people.

questions.question: Which best describes a ziggurat?

choices.A: A flat field used for farming
choices.B: A tall, stepped temple built to honor the gods
choices.C: A river boat used for trade

questions.explanation: A ziggurat was a tall, stepped temple built to honor the gods.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the social groups described in Sumerian society?
questions.explanation: Astronauts were not part of Sumerian society; the groups were kings and priests, merchants and crafters, farmers, and enslaved people.

questions.question: If the priests said the gods wanted a new temple built, what would most likely happen?

choices.A: The people would ignore the priests completely
choices.B: The people would likely obey because priests were believed to speak for the gods
choices.D: The city would be abandoned forever

questions.explanation: People would likely obey because priests were believed to speak for the gods, giving them great influence.

questions.question: The Sumerians made pottery, cloth, and tools. The people who made these goods were called what?
questions.explanation: The people who made pottery, cloth, and tools were crafters.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly compares a king and a farmer in Sumer?

choices.A: A king held great power, while a farmer was part of the largest, lower-ranked group
choices.B: A farmer ruled the city, while a king grew the crops
choices.D: A king was at the bottom and a farmer at the top

questions.explanation: A king held great power, while a farmer belonged to the largest, lower-ranked group.

questions.question: Why did the Sumerians build their ziggurats so tall?

choices.A: To hide the city from view
choices.B: To store extra grain in the basement
choices.C: To block the river from flooding
choices.D: To honor the gods and make the temple stand out as the most important place

questions.explanation: Ziggurats were built tall to honor the gods and stand out as the city's most important place.

questions.question: What is the BEST meaning of the word 'polytheism'?
questions.explanation: 'Polytheism' means belief in many gods.

questions.question: Which sentence BEST summarizes the main idea of 'Religion and Daily Life in Sumer'?

choices.A: Religion shaped Sumerian life, giving kings and priests power and influencing how cities were organized
choices.B: The Sumerians had no gods and no temples
choices.C: Everyone in Sumer had exactly equal power and the same job
choices.D: Religion had no effect on Sumerian cities or rulers

questions.explanation: The main idea is that religion shaped Sumerian life, giving kings and priests power and influencing how cities were organized.
